beats.narration_text: Vanakkam, this is Liam, in for Bear. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, not a transcript. Assignment three: three Blender models for Vidiyum Mun, built by Claude through the Blender M C P, judged by Shriram, and checked in Godot.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about Vidiyum Mun, a time-loop mystery on a fenced private beach on ECR, Chennai, into three game assets built in Blender through the MCP: the SUV whose keys decide the dawn crash, Manimekala's rock shrine, and one segment of the illegal fence. Six basic shapes each, flat colours, exported to Godot.

beats.role_note: One execute_blender_code body, verbatim (tools/blender/build_suv.py, outside godot/; GodotDesignBoard excerpt).
beats.narration_text: Here's one of the calls Claude ran, saved word for word in build S U V dot p y. Add a one metre cube. Name it S U V chassis. Scale it to four point six, by one point eight, by zero point seven five. Apply the scale, so the node stays at one. Then a flat body colour.

props.title: One call Claude ran in Blender
props.excerpt:
root = bpy.data.objects["suv"]
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0.0, 0.0, 0.725))
obj = bpy.context.active_object
obj.name = "SUV_Chassis"
obj.data.name = "SUV_Chassis"
obj.scale = (4.60, 1.80, 0.75)
bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=True, scale=True)
obj.data.materials.clear()
obj.data.materials.append(flat_material("SUV_body", "#2e2d38"))

beats.role_note: Shriram's own hand edit by mouse (recording 20:31–20:36, 16x).
beats.narration_text: Now Shriram's own hand edit, by mouse, sixteen times faster. The fence sign floated between the ropes. Shriram duplicated it twice, then deleted the copies to stay at six shapes, and moved it to the centre, in front. By eye, it sat about five centimetres off the rope. Typing X zero and Y minus zero point zero three put it flush. The lesson, in Shriram's words: front and back depend on the Y axis.

beats.role_note: Self-test: deliberately broken stand-ins. Paired result B09.
beats.narration_text: A check that always passes proves nothing. So the self-test breaks things on purpose: a box stand-in floated half a metre, shrunk to a tenth, laid on its side, a sign colour turned white, a budget squeezed below the triangle count.

show.event: line highlight: lying on its side

props.title: The check must be able to fail
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/tests/check_a3_selftest.gd lines 64–78 · git 81c1666
props.code:
var n := _fence(); n.position.y = 0.5                    # A3-F3: origin in the middle -> floats
	expect("floating by 0.5 m", await _result(n, spec, brief), "base on the floor", false)
	n = _fence(); n.scale = Vector3(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)           # A3-F2/F4: wrong size, unapplied scale
	var by := await _result(n, spec, brief)
	expect("scaled x0.1", by, "size within", false)
	expect("scaled x0.1", by, "every node scale", false)
	n = _fence(); n.rotation_degrees = Vector3(90, 0, 0)     # A3-F1: lying on its side
	by = await _result(n, spec, brief)
	expect("lying on its side", by, "upright", false)
	expect("lying on its side", by, "root not rotated", false)
	n = _fence()                                              # A3-F6: a colour lost in export
	((n.get_child(2) as MeshInstance3D).mesh.material as StandardMaterial3D).albedo_color = Color.WHITE
	expect("sign colour lost", await _result(n, spec, brief), "colour", false)
	var tight := spec.duplicate(true); tight.max_tris = 40    # A3-F5: over budget (4 boxes = 48 tris)
	expect("over the triangle budget", await _result(_fence(), tight, brief), "triangles", false)

notes.label: A3-F1…F7
notes.value: predicted failures, each expected to be caught

notes.label: expect(…, false)
notes.value: a pass here would be a test failure

beats.role_note: Result of B08: actual headless stdout of check_a3_selftest.gd, rendered.
beats.narration_text: Every break is caught. Seventeen of seventeen. One honest scar: the correct stand-in once failed, because it still wore the first brief's steel colours. The stand-in was updated, the assertion was not. And a pass proves size, scale and orientation, not that a model looks right.

beats.role_note: What Claude got wrong + Shriram's look check (TEST-REPORT / FACTS).
beats.narration_text: What Claude got wrong. It priced an icosphere at eighty triangles; it's twenty. It raised the S U V's whole underside when only the nose was meant. It measured the rock at one point one four metres, not one point two. It floated the fence sign, and the export failed twice. Shriram's look check: the shrine looks great. The S U V is fine for six shapes; a real one would be smoother.

props.title: What Claude got wrong
props.excerpt:
Icosphere 'subdivisions 1' priced at 80 tris (it is 20).
SUV build 2 raised the whole underside, not just the nose.
Wheel silver faces didn't apply at first (caught with look).
Rock measured 1.14 m, not 1.20 (stretched).
Fence sign floated between the ropes.
Export failed twice; in Godot the goddess faced the SUV.
Self-test stand-in kept revision-1 colours (1/17 failed).
props.status: REVISION · every fix came from a measurement, a look, a screenshot or Shriram
